tip.en: Clean water to drink comes first. Taps can stop working after a storm.
Food that doesn't spoil (in easy-open cans) keeps your family fed until help comes.
The power often goes out in a typhoon. A flashlight is safer than candles.
Spare batteries keep your flashlight and radio working.
A battery radio brings PAGASA storm news even when the power and phone signal are down.
A first-aid kit lets a grown-up clean and cover small cuts right away.
Pack the medicines your family needs every day.
Copies of IDs and family papers in a waterproof pouch help your family get help.
A charged power bank keeps a phone on, so your family can call for help.
A whistle helps rescuers find you. It is louder than shouting and never gets tired.

why.en: Nice! A raincoat keeps you dry on the way to the evacuation center.

tip.en: If there is room, a raincoat keeps you dry on the way to the evacuation center.

why.en: Nice! A blanket keeps you warm at the evacuation center.

tip.en: If there is room, a blanket keeps you warm at the evacuation center.

why.en: A game console won't keep you safe, and it takes space a first-aid kit needs.
A teddy bear is cosy, but space is tight. Safety things come first.
A TV stand is big, heavy and no help in a storm. It stays home.

tip.en: The baby needs milk and a clean bottle.
Pack enough diapers for the baby for a few days.
Your dog needs food too. Pets come with the family.
Lola's daily medicines can't wait. Pack extra in case you stay away for days.
Tito's wheelchair needs spare batteries so he can keep moving.
Tito's medical papers tell doctors and nurses what care he needs.
